CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for chronic congestive heart failure with diastolic dysfunction and pre-operative evaluation.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
76-year-old female Nicole Miller presenting for follow-up management of chronic CHF with diastolic dysfunction. She previously had an exacerbation of CHF with BNP of 3,000 in March, which increased to 6,000 in April, prompting medication changes. Furosemide was changed to torsemide 20 mg daily, and lisinopril was increased to 10 mg daily. Since the April visit, she has lost approximately 3 to 3.5 pounds and reports significant improvement in dyspnea. She also notes improvement in urinary urgency. Patient is scheduled for right knee replacement surgery on June 24th and wants to ensure her cardiovascular status is optimized prior to the procedure. Recently she experienced bilateral leg cramps, which she attributed to sleeping with a ceiling fan on while cold; symptoms resolved after consuming approximately 4 ounces of pickle juice. She has a history of heartburn that was treated with prilosec for approximately two weeks in January; she has not had any problems since stopping that medication. She is taking an iron supplement and reports good urinary function.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies current dyspnea. Recent bilateral leg cramps, now resolved. Denies current heartburn. Urinary function good. Reports feeling okay overall.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Chronic congestive heart failure with diastolic dysfunction
History of anemia
Right knee pathology requiring replacement

MEDICATIONS
Torsemide 20 mg daily
Lisinopril 10 mg daily
Iron supplement
Clopidogrel (to be discontinued 1 week prior to surgery)

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
No family history of colon cancer. Otherwise not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Married. Has Medicare insurance and private insurance through husband. Uses pickle juice for muscle cramps.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Lungs: Auscultated, sound pretty good.
Breathing: Non-labored, able to take deep breaths.

RESULTS
Hemoglobin: Normal, doing great.
Potassium: 3.9, holding steady on torsemide.
Creatinine: 0.7, appropriate.
BUN: 23, mildly elevated, may indicate mild dehydration but not concerning.
Blood glucose: 169 mg/dL today (non-fasting).
A1C: 5.5 in March.
Magnesium: 1.7 (normal, but goal is around 2.0 for cardiac stabilization).
BNP: March 3,000, April 6,000; current results pending.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Chronic congestive heart failure with mixed presentation: Patient had CHF exacerbation in early spring with elevated BNP. Switched from furosemide to torsemide 20 mg daily with good symptomatic improvement, weight loss of 3 to 3.5 pounds, and non-labored breathing. Will continue current medication regimen. Recommend magnesium supplementation twice daily to help stabilize heart muscle (goal level 2.0). EKG to be repeated today. Labs reviewed show appropriate kidney function. Patient tolerating torsemide well without potassium supplementation. No repeat chest X-ray needed as patient had recent imaging.

2. Pre-operative evaluation: Right knee replacement scheduled for June 24th (end of June). Complete pre-operative check within two weeks of surgery, during first or second week of June. EKG to be repeated today if needed. Clopidogrel to be discontinued 1 week prior to surgery; patient has written reminders and will receive additional reminder from clinic. No chest X-ray needed. No additional blood work needed at this time.

3. Colonoscopy: Patient overdue for screening colonoscopy. Schedule at Bartley Regional Hospital within next 30 days, prior to anticipated change in insurance. No family history of colon cancer. Can be completed prior to surgery without delaying surgery date. Options include Dr. Martin at County Surgical Services or Valley Medical at Springfield, pending availability.

4. Diabetes: A1C was 5.5 in March (adequate control). No repeat A1C ordered today. May need repeat A1C prior to surgery next month. Blood glucose today 169 mg/dL on non-fasting state; may need repeat fasting glucose prior to surgery.
